Article Title: 'Ballot paper, still we ask': Kharge dares BJP to dissolve Parliament after MLC poll setback
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday reiterated the opposition's demand for voting using ballot paper despite the party's lacklustre performance in the Karnataka MLC elections, which were held using ballot papers.Reacting to the Karnataka MLC results, Kharge said the opposition would not give up its demand for ballot paper voting simply because BJP won the elections. He also challenged the BJP to dissolve Parliament and contest elections using ballot papers."Ballot paper, still we ask. It doesn't mean that we should leave because they are winning. Once upon a time they won only two Parliament seats. Sometimes it happens, that doesn't mean that party has no hold," Kharge said."That ego should not be there in BJP that they have done very well. If that is the case, let them dissolve the Parliament and go on ballot paper," he added.Kharge's remarks came after Prime Minister Narendra Modi took a dig at Congress for "drawing a blank" in recent MLC elections. The grand old party had won zero seats till Wednesday night. The party, however, opened its account after retaining Nagpur Division Graduates' constituency seat."MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states - Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?" PM Modi said in a post on X.BJP national president Nitin Nabin also targeted Congress, saying the party would continue to struggle for survival under Rahul Gandhi's leadership. Addressing a gathering during the BJP's ‘Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao’ march in Delhi, Nabin said PM Narendra Modi would return to the Red Fort after the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.Nabin also accused Congress of opposing the revision of electoral rolls because it was distressed by efforts to remove alleged infiltrators.“There are voters who have died but whose names remain on the electoral rolls. There are also people whose names appear in the voter lists at two places. There are crores of such voters whose names are registered more than once, while the whereabouts of many others cannot be traced.This is what is called a ‘ghost voter list’,” he said.The remarks followed the BJP-JD(S) alliance's sweep of all four Karnataka legislative council seats, despite Congress being in power in the state. The results also saw Congress lose its sitting Bengaluru Teachers’ constituency to the JD(S), while the BJP retained three seats.PM Modi's reference to ballot papers comes amid the opposition's repeated allegations of irregularities in electronic voting machines (EVMs) and demands for greater transparency in the electoral process.
Article Summary: Mallikarjun Kharge says opposition will not give up its demand for ballot paper voting. He also challenged the BJP to dissolve Parliament and contest elections using ballot papers. Prime Minister Narendra Modi took a dig at Congress for "drawing a blank" in recent MLC elections.

Article Title: A vitamin clue to stroke in the young? Bengaluru study finds low B6 levels
Article Text:
Vitamin B6 is found in liver, fish such as tuna and salmon, chicken, chickpeas, sunflower seeds, pistachios, potatoes, bananas and spinach.

NEW DELHI: A vitamin that helps the body process proteins and regulate important chemical reactions may offer a new clue to why young adults suffer strokes. A study by researchers in Bengaluru has found significantly lower levels of vitamin B6 in young adults who had an ischaemic stroke than in healthy people of a similar age.Ahead of World Stroke Day on October 29, the findings draw attention to a possible factor associated with stroke in young adults. The study compared 171 young adults who had suffered an ischaemic stroke, caused by a blocked blood vessel in the brain, with 249 healthy controls.Median vitamin B6 levels in stroke patients were 40.9 nmol/L, compared with 65.6 nmol/L in the control group. Vitamin B6 insufficiency, defined by the researchers as levels below 30 nmol/L, was found in 12.3% of stroke patients, compared with just 0.7% of healthy controls.Vitamin B6 is found in liver, fish such as tuna and salmon, chicken, chickpeas, sunflower seeds, pistachios, potatoes, bananas and spinach.Prof Manjari Tripathi, head of the department of neurology at AIIMS, said vitamin B6 is essential for homocysteine metabolism. “Low vitamin B6 levels can impair this process, allowing homocysteine to rise. Elevated homocysteine can damage blood vessels, promote inflammation and contribute to clot formation, increasing stroke risk.Maintaining adequate vitamin B6 levels through a balanced diet is important,” she said.The Bengaluru study adds to evidence linking vitamin B6 levels with stroke risk, but whether improving these levels can prevent strokes remains unclear. Dr Pravin Gupta, chairman, Marengo Asia international institute of neuro and spine, said the study was significant because vitamin B6 levels can be measured through a blood test. “However, this study shows an association, not proof that vitamin B6 supplements can prevent stroke. Further research is needed,” he said.The researchers, led by scientists from the National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (NIMHANS), Bengaluru, found that lower vitamin B6 levels were independently associated with higher odds of ischaemic stroke even after accounting for other factors. Among stroke patients, vitamin B6 levels were strongly inversely correlated with homocysteine, an amino acid associated with blood vessel health.Published inin 2026, the case-control study adds to research into factors associated with stroke among younger adults. However, it cannot establish whether low vitamin B6 contributes to stroke, results from other health or dietary factors, or reflects an underlying process. Further studies are needed to validate the findings.The results do not establish that vitamin B6 supplements can prevent stroke or that routine testing for the vitamin should be recommended for young adults.
Article Summary: Vitamin B6 is found in liver, fish such as tuna and salmon, chicken, chickpeas, sunflower seeds, pistachios, potatoes, bananas and spinach. Researchers in Bengaluru found significantly lower levels of vitamin B6 in young adults who had an ischaemic stroke.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Thursday took a dig at BJP supporters for flagging the misspelling of Union minister Nirmala Sitharaman 's name in a social media post by Rahul Gandhi , saying the deliberate typo was a strategy to draw attention.In a post on X, Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate thanked BJP supporters for amplifying Rahul Gandhi's post in which he accused the government of “criminally destroying” the Tata Group ."BJP buffoons fall prey so easily. In communication, deliberate misspelling is a strategy to gain attention. It’s called Typo Marketing," the Congress leader said."Thank you for amplifying Rahul ji’s tweet on Tata by desperately pointing out Sitaraman misspelt. Rahul alleged that no business leader dared to speak out against the alleged interference.In a post on X, the Congress leader said, "Tata is being criminally destroyed, and no business leader dares say a word.How long will you stay silent? Until they own you?" He added that Indian businesses were not Prime Minister Narendra Modi's and home minister Amit Shah's "plaything" and accused business leaders of lacking the courage to speak out.Sitharaman hit back at Rahul, accusing him of trying to incite business leaders to join him in spreading "distrust and toxicity". She urged him to refrain from politicising every issue and said casually labelling commercial and legal matters as criminal was unacceptable.Defending the government's policies, Sitharaman said the Modi government valued Indian industry as a source of jobs and economic growth. She also accused the Congress of having stifled Indian entrepreneurs for decades through the "Licence-Quota Raj" and said the government's policies were designed to support enterprise, industry and investment.Responding with another X post, Rahul wrote, "Dear Mrs. Sitarama (sic), 1. Which 'legal and commercial matter' required Tata Trusts and Tata Sons to be hosted at Amit Shah's residence? 2. When is crony number 1 going to appear in the game and which pieces of Tata is he going to get?""Finally, all India's businesses except 3-4 of your cronies already hate all of you and don't need any incitement," he added.The Congress leader's remarks come against the backdrop of a dispute over Tata Sons' leadership. Earlier this week, Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata challenged the September 17 board resolution of Tata Sons to reappoint N Chandrasekaran as chairman of the holding company of the country's largest conglomerate.

Article Title: Thousands of years of knowledge, struggle shaped India as cultural nation: Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
Article Text:
Sekhawat was addressing a gathering at the launch of the book 'Timeless India: Protection & Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the Leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi'

NEW DELHI: Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat on Wednesday said India is not merely an entity confined within geographical boundaries but a cultural nation shaped by thousands of years of continuity, knowledge, struggle and experience.Shekhawat was addressing a gathering at the launch of the book 'Timeless India: Protection & Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the Leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi' at the Dharohar Bhawan, the headquarters of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), which hosted the event along with the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA).The book has been published by IGNCA and Subhi Publications and edited by former Rajya Sabha member Tarun Vijay."India is not merely an entity confined within geographical boundaries, but a cultural nation shaped by thousands of years of continuity, knowledge, spiritual practice, struggle and experience. India's civilisation and cultural consciousness have flowed uninterrupted through centuries," Shekhawat said."India has established connections with civilisations across the world through dialogue and cultural exchange.Its knowledge traditions, architectural heritage and cultural legacy have attracted many countries around the world," he added.During the colonial rule, "efforts were made to weaken Indians' sense of pride" in their civilisation, culture and traditions. This also influenced the way Indians viewed their own knowledge traditions and cultural ideals, an IGNCA statement quoted the minister as saying."The distinctive feature of Indian civilisation is its ability to draw inspiration from the past while moving towards the future. Ideals represented by Lord Ram and Lord Krishna, along with the traditions of sages, thinkers and seekers of knowledge, remain important foundations for India's cultural consciousness," he said.The book explores the role of monuments in preserving and revitalising India's cultural identity, alongside the discourse surrounding the nation's historical memory.It gives particular importance to monument preservation and the idea of "decolonising the nation's memory", highlighting the need to understand India's cultural heritage through its "own historical experiences, traditions and cultural outlook", the statement said.Union Minister of State Jitendra Singh, former Rajya Sabha member and ex-president of the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), Vinay Sahasrabuddhe, were present on the occasion, among others.In a separate statement, the tourism ministry said the Indian Culinary Institute (ICI) on Wednesday signed an MoU with the Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), providing for the recognition of ICI's BBA and MBA programmes by the JNU, enabling the university to award degrees to students completing these courses at ICI.The MoU was signed by JNU V-C Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit and Gyan Bhushan, Director, ICI, in the presence of Shekhawat and Tourism Secretary Bhuvnesh Kumar.The recognition of ICI's BBA and MBA programmes by JNU, commencing from the next academic year, is expected to enhance academic and professional opportunities for the students, the statement said.
Article Summary: Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said India is a cultural nation shaped by thousands of years of continuity, knowledge, struggle and experience. He was addressing a gathering at the launch of the book 'Timeless India: Protection & Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the Leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi'

DITE DIME: Anti-dam protests have prompted a major security build-up at the Dite-Dime bridge in Arunachal Pradesh, a key crossing towards the India-China border that connects four proposed drilling sites for a pre-feasibility survey of the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project.Forces have heavily fortified the bridge, deploying large numbers of CAPF personnel, as it has become a focal point of the anti-dam movement, hosting dharnas and protests against the proposed survey. Officials said 30 companies of CAPF had been deployed across protest-hit districts. At least four women were wounded in a clash at Dite-Dime on Oct 23 during a 12-hour bandh. More than 150 supporters allegedly threw stones at security personnel, tried to breach barricades and damaged security vehicles, police sources said.

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Thursday took stock of the impact of cyclone Arnab and spoke to the chief ministers of Andhra Pradesh , Puducherry, Odisha and Chhattisgarh; adding that centre will give all assistance and relief operations are on "War footing"."In the wake of Cyclone Arnab, spoke with the Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry, Odisha and Chhattisgarh and assured them of every assistance to mitigate the hardship of the people in the face of the disaster," he said in a post on X.Further giving info on rescue and relief, he added, " NDRF and SDRF teams have sprung into action and are continuing rescue and relief operations on a war footing. NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Congress on Thursday took a swipe at chief minister Devendra Fadnavis after the party retained the Nagpur Graduates’ constituency in the legislative council elections. The final result, which came after more than 40 hours of counting, forced Fadnavis to delete a tweet he had posted the previous day, mocking the Congress for failing to win any seat in the MLC polls.On Wednesday, PM Modi had posted a tweet mocking the Congress for failing to open its account despite the elections being held using ballot papers.The Congress had reacted sharply and dared to hold all elections using ballot papers, asking how many seats the party had won.Congress candidate and sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJP's Sudhakar Kohale in the Nagpur Graduates’ constituency by 3,271 votes, securing 67,231 votes against his rival's 63,960.Also read - 'Commit to ballot paper': Congress dares PM Modi after his 'how many seats' swipe over MLC results Fadnavis had posted the tweet in response to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s dig at the Congress on X.“By deleting the tweet, Fadnavis has once again preserved Savarkar's legacy! Even before the full results were in hand, in a show of firing a big arrow, Fadnavis tweeted.But that very arrow turned back and pierced straight into his chest! In the end, he was forced to delete the tweet,” the Maharashtra Congress said on X.“Mr. Fadnavis, scared already at this stage? This is just the trailer! In 2029, the people of Maharashtra will drop such a political bombshell on you that even this tweet of today will come back to haunt you! All the best, Mr. Fadnavis! Get ready for the next jolt,” it added.Wanjari, the sitting MLC, secured 67,231 votes against Kohale's 63,960. The result dealt a setback to the BJP in Nagpur, the hometown of Fadnavis and Union minister Nitin Gadkari, both of whom had campaigned extensively for Kohale.The Congress also targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks on the party's performance in the Legislative Council elections held across four states. Modi had questioned the Congress's tally, pointing out that the polls were conducted using ballot papers."MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states - Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?" Modi wrote in a post on X.Congress Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera responded by challenging the prime minister to commit to using ballot papers in future Lok Sabha and assembly elections."If Narendra Modi is so confident that EVMs have no bearing on election results, let him prove his confidence in the BJP’s electoral prowess through action, not rhetoric," Khera wrote on X.He also demanded the suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the restoration of what he alleged were 13.3 crore illegally deleted voters, and action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar also criticised Fadnavis over the deleted post, pointing to the BJP's defeat in Nagpur, where the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) headquarters is located."Respected Devendra Fadnavis Saheb, In the Nagpur Graduates Constituency, where you yourself took personal interest and went door-to-door to persuade the rebels to withdraw, in that very Nagpur constituency, in the area where the RSS headquarters is located, the BJP had to face defeat—the meaning of this is clear…… It is indeed regrettable that you had to delete your tweet; but the immense ego of power evident in your deleted tweet is not good at all. Anyway, I can understand. Perhaps you forgot that the election was held via ballot, so the tweet might have been made prematurely… Congratulations to the victorious candidate Abhijit Wanjarri, thanks to the graduates who gave their blessings in the form of votes, and best wishes to all the contesting candidates as well!" Pawar wrote on X.With Wanjari's victory, the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) won three of the five Maharashtra Legislative Council seats contested on October 23, while the BJP-led Mahayuti secured two.NCP (SP) candidates Harshada Deshmukh-Jadhav and Pratapsinh Patil won the Pune Graduates’ and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Graduates’ constituencies, respectively. Shiv Sena candidate Kiran Sarnaik won the Amravati Teachers’ constituency, while BJP candidate Kaustubh Gawade secured the Pune Teachers’ seat.The Nagpur result followed more than 40 hours of counting. Kohale had led Wanjari after the second round, but neither candidate secured the required quota through first-preference votes. Wanjari eventually overtook his rival during the subsequent elimination rounds as preferential votes were transferred.The outcome dealt a setback to the BJP in a constituency it had traditionally held. Gadkari represented the Nagpur Graduates’ constituency in the Maharashtra Legislative Council for 24 years, from 1990 to 2014.The results have triggered a political exchange between the BJP and opposition parties over electoral performance and the use of electronic voting machines. While Modi cited the ballot-paper polls to question the Congress's performance, the party has used the results to renew its demand for ballot papers in future elections.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Congress took a swipe at chief minister Devendra Fadnavis after the party retained the Nagpur Graduates’ constituency in the legislative council elections. The final result came after more than 40 hours of counting. The Congress also targeted PM Narendra Modi over his remarks on the party's performance in the Legislative Council elections held across four states.

Article Title: Oil prices slip as peace hopes ease supply fears, Middle East tensions limit losses
Article Text:
Crude prices relax

Houthi attacks keep supply concerns alive

Conflicting signals from US-Iran peace efforts

Oil prices declined on Thursday as traders weighed the possibility of fresh diplomatic developments between the US and Iran against the risk of further supply disruptions from escalating attacks in the Middle East.Brent crude fell by $0.85, or 0.74%, to $114.50 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropped $0.91, or 0.89%, to $101.90. The decline pared gains made in the previous session, when Brent advanced 1.3% and WTI climbed 3%.The prospect of a diplomatic breakthrough emerged after US vice president JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei in an effort to restart peace negotiations, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing US officials and people familiar with the matter.The possibility of further negotiations has offered some relief to oil markets, but the threat of an intensification in regional hostilities continues to weigh on the outlook for supplies. Concerns include renewed attacks by Yemen's Houthis and the possibility that the US could launch an attack on Iran after its mid-term elections on November 3.Fresh developments in the conflict involving the Houthis and Saudi Arabia added to uncertainty on Thursday.The Saudi-led coalition fighting the group said it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired towards the kingdom's eastern region early in the day, with hostilities between the two sides showing no signs of easing.The latest incident followed an attack on Aden airport on Wednesday, according to Yemeni government forces. A day earlier, the Houthis had said they struck Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery with a missile, escalating their attacks against the world's second-largest crude producer after the United States.Saudi authorities had not immediately confirmed the reported strike on the refinery, which has a capacity of 550,000 barrels per day.The continuing attacks have kept concerns over potential supply disruptions in focus even as diplomatic efforts offer the possibility of easing tensions.Efforts to find a way to end the war involving the US, Israel and Iran have produced mixed signals. An official briefed on the negotiations said Qatari mediators had presented Iran with a new draft agreement to end the conflict.However, a senior Iranian official rejected the proposals, describing them as unacceptable ideas that did not constitute an offer.Iran's foreign minister said on Wednesday that Tehran was continuing to give diplomacy a chance to succeed. The minister also flagged the possibility of completing Iran's seven-day plan in less than a week if it was adopted.The contrasting positions leave the prospects for a diplomatic resolution uncertain, while the possibility of renewed negotiations has contributed to the downward movement in crude prices.Meanwhile, US inventory data provided another factor for oil markets to follow. The US Energy Information Administration said that energy companies had withdrawn 1.9 million barrels of crude oil from storage during the week ended October 23.Gasoline inventories, however, increased by 3.9 million barrels, against analysts' expectations of a decline of 900,000 barrels.The opposing movements in crude and gasoline stockpiles added to the mixed signals facing oil markets as traders assessed the impact of diplomatic developments, regional attacks and US inventory data on prices.
Article Summary: Brent crude fell by 0.74%, to $114.50 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropped $0.91, or 0.89%. The decline pared gains made in the previous session, when Brent advanced 1.3% and WTI climbed 3%. The prospect of a diplomatic breakthrough emerged after US vice president JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei.

Article Title: ‘Unwavering commitment’: Rajnath Singh backs ASEAN centrality, calls for stronger defence ties

Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday reaffirmed India’s commitment to ASEAN centrality and called for stronger defence cooperation and mutual trust at the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, Philippines.“India reiterates its unwavering commitment to ASEAN centrality, which is a cornerstone of our Act East Policy and Indo-Pacific vision,” Singh said, expressing gratitude to the Philippines for hosting the meeting and extending warm hospitality.He said the forum was important for maintaining a resilient, secure and prosperous region, adding that the discussions should help address emerging disruptions and strengthen cooperation among participating countries.“I look forward to constructive deliberations and concrete outcomes from this meeting,” Singh said.Philippine defence secretary Gilberto C Teodoro Jr, meanwhile, said two documents were signed at the ADMM the previous day — a joint statement commemorating the 50th anniversary of the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia and the Manila Joint Declaration marking the 20th anniversary of the ADMM.Teodoro said the documents reaffirmed the participating countries’ commitment to shared principles, ASEAN unity and centrality.He outlined three priorities for the meeting: ensuring cooperation is guided by mutual respect and international law, sustaining progress under the ADMM-Plus framework, and addressing the wider impact of global disruptions.Highlighting the importance of food and energy security amid supply chain challenges and overseas conflicts, Teodoro also called for greater cooperation to protect migrant workers and seafarers, particularly those from smaller countries caught in conflict zones.He said the international order had a special obligation to protect migrant workers and seafarers, recognising their contribution to the global economy and the countries in which they work.“Together, let us create a safer and more prosperous future for our region and the world,” Teodoro said.
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh called for stronger defence cooperation and mutual trust at the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, Philippines. He said the forum was important for maintaining a resilient, secure and prosperous region.

NEW DELHI: Former Tamil Nadu chief minister and DMK president M K Stalin on Thursday accused the C Joseph Vijay-led Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government of using vigilance raids as political theatre ahead of the Tiruchirappalli East by-election. Stalin also asserted that the searches would not intimidate DMK workers.The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) on Thursday conducted searches at 25 locations across Tamil Nadu linked to former minister and DMK leader K N Nehru in connection with an alleged Rs 634-crore cash-for-jobs scam involving recruitment in the Municipal Administration and Water Supply (MAWS) department.In a post on X, Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK)chief Stalin described the action as “Vettri Vendetta Politics” and accused the state government of attempting to divert attention from law-and-order concerns.“The Chief Minister, who has turned Tamil Nadu into a state where women, children, and the elderly are no longer safe, is now contemplating whether to conduct a 'Roadshow' or a 'Raidshow' to divert the attention of the people and the media's 'Breaking News',” Stalin said.The DMK chief also accused the ruling party of selectively targeting former ministers while inducting leaders facing corruption allegations.“TVK, a 'TN Branch Washing Machine' that is turning all the corrupt vermin into 'bargaining horses' and inducting them into its party, is pursuing a plan of 'Vettri Vendetta Politics' by targeting only the former ministers of the DMK regime.As always, this will fail before the law and hang its head in shame before the public!” he said.Linking the searches to the upcoming by-election, Stalin alleged that the operation was intended to generate social media content and provide Vijay with political talking points.“These raids, conducted to produce 'Reels' for the Tiruchirappalli East by-election and to allow the Chief Minister to scream on stage in various modulations under the guise of 'punch dialogues,' will not make even the toenail of the lowermost DMK cadre tremble!” he said.The DVAC searches follow the registration of a case against Nehru and others after the Madras High Court directed a probe into alleged irregularities flagged by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). The allegations concern bribes collected from candidates in exchange for government postings during Nehru’s tenure as minister.The agency is examining documents and financial records to trace the suspected money trail and establish evidence relating to the recruitment process.Nehru has also moved the Supreme Court through a special leave petition challenging the Madras High Court’s October 26 order dismissing his review petition against the registration of the first information report (FIR).Stalin further criticised the government over rising prices and governance, saying, “The entire nation, not just Tamil Nadu, is mocking this TVK government, which is plaguing the people with lawlessness, a rusted administration, and scorching price hikes.”
Article Summary: Former Tamil Nadu chief minister M K Stalin accused the C Joseph Vijay-led Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government of using vigilance raids as political theatre. Article Title: Supreme Court removes October 30 deadline for additions to Delhi electoral roll
Article Text:
Supreme Court asked the Election Commission not to stop adding names to Delhi's electoral rolls by the October 30 deadline

How can you insist on Form 6 for person who was voter earlier: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a relief to over 43 lakh voters excluded from Delhi’s draft electoral rolls for ‘permanently shifting out’, Supreme Court on Wednesday asked Election Commission not to stop adding names in the voter list by the Oct 30 deadline and told it to continue distributing and receiving enumeration forms, and Forms 6 (new voters), 7 (for deletion) and 8 (for those who shifted from one constituency to another).A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also questioned EC on why voters whose names were there on earlier electoral rolls but were deleted from the draft rolls were asked to file Form 6, which is meant for enrolment of first-time voters.Without passing any order, the bench said, “We will examine the issue after two weeks. The effort should be to reduce the 43 lakh (who have been deleted from draft rolls). One suggestion — publish the list of those who are deleted and specify the reason for deletion against each name. Request them to contact the nearest BLO and fill Form 8. You can give them enumeration forms. Tell them that they are welcome to fill either Form 6 or 8. ”During the proceedings on a PIL filed by activist Anjali Bhardwaj, the bench heard advocate Prashant Bhushan’s complaints against EC for insisting on filling Form 6 by those whose names got excluded and, thereby, compelling them to give a false declaration that they were first-time voters.The bench said, “Right to vote is a vital right. If a person has shifted out from Vasant Kunj to Dwarka, or had gone out of station for a month or so and for some other reason could not respond to the EC notice or could not file the claim for inclusion of name, or did not get enumeration form because of change of address, should EC permanently disable him from voting by striking his name off the voter list?“How can you insist on Form 6 for a person who was a voter earlier? If a person has shifted from one constituency to another within Delhi, it is erroneous to ask him/her to fill Form 6. You must allow similarly placed persons, whose names are deleted on the ground of ‘permanently shifted’, to fill Form 8.”Appearing for EC, senior advocate D S Naidu said the commission had conducted over one lakh camps in Delhi to spread awareness among people on how to re-enter their names in the voter list.“The situation on the ground is very different. Not a single person has come to fill Form 8. The petitioner is creating a scare on paper in the courtroom. Any person can seek inclusion of his/her name in the voter list of a constituency till the date of filing of nominations,” Naidu said, and clarified that no one has been prosecuted for using Form 6 to restore names in voter lists across states.But EC relented to keep the window open for inclusion of names in Delhi as SC insisted that the Oct 30 deadline for filing claims and objections need not be set in stone as elections were not imminent in Delhi to warrant urgent completion of the SIR exercise.
Article Summary: Supreme Court asked the Election Commission not to stop adding names to Delhi's electoral rolls by the October 30 deadline. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also questioned EC on why voters whose names were there on earlier electoral rolls but were deleted from draft rolls were asked to file Form 6.

Can you use banking services on a bank holiday?

NEW DELHI: Planning a quick trip to the bank today? You might want to check the holiday calendar first.The festive season brings a fresh round of bank holidays, but closures are not the same across India, as they depend on the festivals and regional occasions observed in each state.Today, October 29, banks in Himachal Pradesh are closed for Karwa Chauth. But if you are elsewhere in the country, the holiday schedule may be different. Therefore, a quick check before stepping out for your bank related errands could save you an unnecessary trip to the branch.After the Karwa Chauth holiday in Himachal Pradesh on October 29, Gujarat is set to see bank closures on October 31 to mark Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary.Bank customers will also need to keep track of the holidays scheduled for November, when several festivals and regional observances are expected to affect branch operations in different states. The list includes Diwali and related celebrations, Ningol Chakkouba, Wangala Festival, Chhath Puja, Igas-Bagwal, Seng Kut Snem, Guru Nanak Jayanti and Kanakadasa Jayanthi.The dates and closures will vary depending on the state and the festival being observed.Bank customers need to check the schedule for their location, as closures depend on the regional festival or occasion being observed.Apart from festival-related closures, scheduled and non-scheduled banks also observe holidays on the second and fourth Saturdays of every month, in line with the Reserve Bank of India's holiday schedule.A branch closure does not mean customers lose access to all banking services. ATMs, Unified Payments Interface (UPI), internet banking and mobile banking applications remain available for routine transactions, including fund transfers, bill payments and account management.The main inconvenience is for transactions that require a visit to a physical branch. Customers planning large cash deposits, cheque processing, demand drafts or other branch-dependent work may have to wait until their branch reopens.With several holidays scheduled across October and November, checking the applicable state calendar before visiting a branch can help customers plan their banking requirements and avoid delays.
Article Summary: The festive season brings a fresh round of bank holidays, but closures are not the same across India. Closures depend on the festivals and regional occasions observed in each state. The dates and closures will vary depending on the state and the festival being observed. A branch closure does not mean customers lose access to all banking services.

BJP-led NDA won 16 of 28 seats in MLC polls held across four states, sweeping all four Karnataka legislative council constituencies, dealing a setback to Congress. Bihar and Maharashtra delivered split verdicts, while BJP led in UP as counting of paper ballots continued from Tuesday till late Wednesday.In Karnataka, JD(S) wrested Bengaluru teachers from Congress, while BJP won North East teachers, West graduates and South East graduates. D K Shivakumar, facing his first polls as CM, said Congress would take corrective measures. “We respect the verdict. We had expected two seats, but that did not happen,” he said.Congress had demanded a return to ballot papers.But results suggested its setbacks stemmed from organisational weaknesses. Party insiders said 19 ministers assigned to oversee 133 assembly segments failed to deliver, amid growing internal differences. BJP and JD(S) coordinated more closely than in previous polls.In Bihar, NDA won four of eight seats, while RJD and Prashant Kishor’s Jan Suraaj won one each. Independents took the remaining two. All four sitting teachers’ constituency MLCs lost, while incumbents retained all four graduates’ seats.RJD-backed Sanjeev Kumar defeated BJP veteran Nawal Yadav, a five-term MLC who had held Patna teachers for three decades. Jan Suraaj’s Suresh Prasad Rai defeated former Bihar Congress chief Madan Mohan Jha by 324 votes in Darbhanga teachers, giving Kishor’s party its first council seat and ending CPI’s lone representation.In UP, BJP won six seats and SP three among nine seats declared by Wednesday evening. Counting continued in Lucknow and Varanasi graduates’ constituencies. Independent Dhruv Tripathi, who later joined BJP, won Gorakhpur-Faizabad teachers for a fourth consecutive term, defeating Independent Rajiv Yadav by 307 votes.Maharashtra’s five MLC seats were closely contested between Mahayuti and opposition alliance MVA, with both winning two each. A large number of votes were declared invalid, which is a matter of concern.”

JD(S) wrested Bengaluru teachers from Congress. All four sitting teachers’ constituency MLCs lost. incumbents retained all four graduates’ seats.

Article Title: MLC election results: NDA wins 16, Congress gets 1, SP bags 5; state-wise results and key wins
Article Text:
The biennial elections for these Graduate and Teacher constituencies across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, and Maharashtra were held via ballot papers on October 23, 2026, with counting beginning on October 27, 2026.

Here is a state-wise look at the latest results and counting trends.

Karnataka (4 seats): BJP-JD(S) alliance sweeps all four, Congress draws blank

Uttar Pradesh (11 seats): BJP wins four seats, SP secures two

Bihar (8 seats): Jan Suraaj opens account, RJD defeats BJP veteran

Maharashtra (5 seats): Congress retains Nagpur graduates’ seat, defeats BJP

NEW DELHI: Congress faced a major setback in the legislative council elections on Wednesday, failing to secure a victory in the seats declared so far across Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Maharashtra, even as counting continued in several constituencies.The biggest setback for the Congress came in Karnataka, where it failed to win a single seat despite being in power in the state. The BJP -JD(S) alliance swept all four legislative council seats, with the BJP retaining three constituencies and the JD(S) wresting the Bengaluru Teachers’ seat from the Congress. The defeat was particularly significant for the ruling party as it lost its sitting seat in Bengaluru Teachers’ and failed to make gains in any of the three BJP-held constituencies.In Uttar Pradesh, the BJP and Samajwadi Party (SP) registered wins, while in Bihar, Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj Party opened its legislative council account by defeating the Congress. The RJD also scored a victory in Bihar, wresting the Patna Teachers’ seat from the BJP.Counting for 28 legislative council seats across Uttar Pradesh (11), Bihar (8), Maharashtra (5) and Karnataka (4) began on Tuesday following polling on October 23.The elections were held for graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies, with results declared for several seats and counting continuing in others.The BJP-JD(S) alliance swept all four legislative council seats in Karnataka, dealing a setback to the ruling Congress. The BJP retained the North-East Teachers’, South-East Graduates’ and West Graduates’ constituencies, while its ally JD(S) wrested the Bengaluru Teachers’ seat from the Congress.JD(S) candidate A P Ranganath defeated sitting Congress MLC Puttanna by 908 votes in Bengaluru Teachers’. Ranganath secured 10,810 votes against Puttanna’s 9,902.BJP’s Shashil G Namoshi retained North-East Teachers’ by 3,297 votes, securing his fifth victory from the constituency with 15,596 votes against Congress candidate Sharanappa Mattur’s 12,299.In South-East Graduates’, BJP candidate K M Suresh defeated Congress nominee Shashi Hulikunte Mutt by 23,098 votes. Sitting BJP MLC S V Sankanur retained West Graduates’, defeating Congress candidate Mohan Limbikai by 9,323 votes.The results marked a clean sweep for the opposition alliance, with the Congress failing to win a single seat despite campaigning by chief minister D K Shivakumar, former chief minister Siddaramaiah and other senior leaders.However, the results are not expected to affect the stability of the Congress government or significantly alter the balance of power in the 75-member Legislative Council.The BJP won six of the 11 Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council seats, while the Samajwadi Party secured five. The BJP won the Agra Graduates’, Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’, Lucknow Teachers’, Meerut Teachers’, Meerut Graduates’ and Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers’ constituencies.The Samajwadi Party won the Allahabad-Jhansi Graduates’, Varanasi Teachers’ and Agra-Aligarh Teachers’ constituencies.In the Agra Graduates’ constituency, BJP candidate Manvendra Pratap Singh (Guruji) was declared elected.The BJP retained the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’ seat, with its candidate Hari Singh Dhillon defeating SP nominee Danish Akhtar by 17,676 votes. Dhillon secured 21,672 votes against Akhtar’s 3,996 after all five rounds of counting.The BJP also won the Lucknow Teachers’ constituency, where its candidate Umesh Dwivedi defeated SP’s Sushil Kumar by 6,992 votes. Dwivedi secured 13,179 votes against Kumar’s 8,371.In Meerut, the BJP won both the Teachers’ and Graduates’ constituencies. Its candidates Dinesh Kumar Goyal and Shri Chand Sharma were declared winners in the Graduates’ and Teachers’ seats, respectively.The BJP also retained the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers’ constituency, with its candidate Dhruv Tripathi defeating Independent candidate Rajiv Yadav by 307 votes. Tripathi secured 14,887 votes against Yadav’s 14,580.However, Yadav alleged that the election had been manipulated to ensure his defeat. Claiming that around 1,000 votes had been stolen, he said he would approach the Election Commission and the court to challenge the result. He also demanded a forensic examination of 1,612 votes counted in the fourth round, alleging irregularities in the counting process.The MLC polls are being viewed as a prestige battle between the ruling BJP and the opposition SP ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Voting for the 11 seats, comprising five Graduates’ and six Teachers’ constituencies, was held on Friday, with counting beginning at 8 am on Tuesday.The Bihar Legislative Council elections delivered several upsets, with five sitting MLCs losing their seats and the Jan Suraaj Party securing its maiden victory in the Upper House.Of the eight seats, which went to polls on October 23, the BJP won three, Independents secured two, while the RJD, Jan Suraaj Party and NDA partner JD(U) won one seat each.Jan Suraaj Party candidate Suresh Prasad Rai defeated sitting Congress MLC Madan Mohan Jha in the Darbhanga Teachers’ constituency, marking the party’s first win in the Bihar Legislative Council.BJP candidate Narendra Prasad Singh won the Tirhut Teachers’ seat, defeating CPI MLC Sanjay Kumar Singh, who had the support of the INDIA bloc.In another major upset, RJD candidate Sanjeev Kumar defeated veteran BJP MLC Nawal Kishore Yadav in the Patna Teachers’ constituency, ending the latter’s long hold on the seat.Independent candidate Rahul Raj also defeated sitting MLC Afaq Ahmed in the Saran Teachers’ constituency.Meanwhile, JD(U)’s Neeraj Kumar retained the Patna Graduates’ seat for a fourth consecutive term, defeating his rivals despite a challenge from within his party. BJP candidates Sarvesh Kumar and N K Yadav retained the Darbhanga Graduates’ and Kosi Graduates’ seats, respectively.Independent candidate Bansi Dhar Brajwasi also retained the Tirhut Graduates’ constituency, while two other seats went to the BJP and Independents as part of the overall tally.The Congress, which contested five seats, failed to win any and is now left with just one member in the 75-member Bihar Legislative Council.The polls saw 90 candidates contesting four Graduates’ constituencies and 60 candidates in four Teachers’ constituencies. The four Graduates’ seats had 4.92 lakh eligible voters, while the four Teachers’ constituencies had 40,253 voters.The BJP-led ruling Mahayuti won two seats in Maharashtra, while the opposition NCP (SP) bagged two, as results were declared for all five Legislative Council seats.Congress candidate and sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJP’s Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes to retain the Nagpur Division Graduates’ constituency, ending more than 40 hours of counting. Wanjari secured 67,231 votes against Kohale’s 63,960.Also read: Congress opens account in MLC polls as Abhijit Wanjari retains Nagpur seat after nail-biting contest Kohale, a former MLA, had led Wanjari by 4,294 votes after the second round of counting on Wednesday. However, with no candidate securing the required quota through first-preference votes, the counting proceeded to second-preference votes, allowing Wanjari to overtake his rival during the elimination rounds.Shiv Sena candidate Kiran Sarnaik won the Amravati Teachers’ constituency, while BJP candidate Kaustubh Gawade emerged victorious in the Pune Teachers’ constituency.In the Pune Graduates’ constituency, NCP (SP) candidate Harshada Deshmukh-Jadhav won, while party candidate Pratapsinh Patil secured victory in the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) Graduates’ constituency.The polls, held on October 23, saw 182 candidates contesting across three Graduates’ and two Teachers’ constituencies. The results were closely watched amid rebel candidates, alliance differences and efforts by the BJP-led Mahayuti and the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi to consolidate support.
Article Summary: BJP-JD(S) alliance sweeps all four legislative council seats in Karnataka. RJD also scored a victory in Bihar, wresting the Patna Teachers’ seat from the BJP. In Uttar Pradesh, the BJP and Samajwadi Party (SP) registered wins.

Article Title: 'Battle scars': Massive stitches on Captain Smit Machchhar head draw attention as UAE honours hero Indian pilot

A massive line of stitches running across the back of Captain Smit Machchhar’s head has brought the severity of the Indian pilot’s injuries into focus as he received a prestigious UAE honour for his role in thwarting the mid-air cockpit attack.Far-right UK leader Tommy Robinson shared a photograph of the scar on social media, praising Machchhar for his bravery. “Not all heroes wear capes. Some wear battle scars. Hero Indian Captain Smit Machchhar. The world salutes you,” Robinson wrote.The Indian captain and his fellow flydubai crew members were conferred the First Class Order of Zayed II by UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in recognition of their efforts to protect passengers during the September 30 incident aboard flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv.The medals were presented by Dubai Crown Prince Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum at a presidential reception. The UAE leadership praised the crew for their courage, professionalism and commitment to passenger safety.Machchhar was seriously injured when his co-pilot allegedly attacked him with a crash axe and stabbed him inside the cockpit. The aircraft, carrying more than 170 people, reportedly plunged nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds during the incident.Despite being covered in blood and severely wounded, Machchhar managed to release the cockpit door lock, allowing passengers and crew members to overpower the co-pilot. Two other flydubai pilots who were travelling on board then took control of the aircraft and landed it safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.The motive behind the alleged attack remains unclear. The co-pilot, identified by Israeli officials as an Omani national, was taken into custody.Machchhar was initially treated at a hospital in Tabuk before being transferred to Abu Dhabi for further treatment. Sheikh Hamdan had earlier visited him in hospital and praised his courage in helping avert a potential tragedy.The First Class Order of Zayed II is a high-level UAE civil decoration awarded in recognition of distinguished service and exceptional contributions. The honour recognises the crew's actions in protecting the lives of those aboard the aircraft.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar was seriously injured when his co-pilot allegedly attacked him with a crash axe and stabbed him inside the cockpit. The Indian captain and his fellow flydubai crew members were conferred the First Class Order of Zayed II by UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. The UAE leadership praised the crew for their courage, professionalism and commitment to passenger safety.

NEW DELHI: Striking a discordant note among a clutch of petitions challenging the Transgender Amendment Act for denying right to gender self-determination, an all-women NGO Wednesday appealed to the Supreme Court not to confer trans-women, biological males identifying as females, the spectrum of constitutional rights guaranteed to biological women.‘Women’s Declaration International India’ through senior advocate Amit Sibal told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that “self-professed or socio-cultural gender identity or certificate or document cannot change a person’s biological sex or enable a biological male to access the entire spectrum of rights, protections and entitlements created specifically for biological females. ” Differentiating between sex and gender, the petitioner said, “Sex and gender identity are distinct; gender identity concerns a person’s deeply felt internal experience, while sex is the stable immutable biological category on which numerous constitutional and statutory protections for women are premised.”SC asked Centre to respond to the petition with a comprehensive affidavit that also dealt with the other petitions challenging the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026.SG Tushar Mehta said a comprehensive affidavit is being drafted but gave an indication of what would be govt’s stand in defence of the erasure of gender self-determination clause, which was replaced by medically determined gender.He asked: “Can a transwoman be permitted to compete in a sporting event for women? Should a policewoman conduct physical search of a person with male genitals but perceives himself to be a woman? If a biologically male criminal perceives himself to be a woman, should police be barred from arresting him after sunset?”Drawing the court’s attention to a recent incident in the US relating to a transgender inmate, who perceives himself to be a woman but impregnated two women inmates, Mehta said several aspects needed to be kept in mind while adjudicating the petitions.A male becoming a trans-woman will violate affirmative measures for women under the Constitution, equal opportunity to women in employment, women’s bodily privacy and personal security in sex-segregated spaces and criminal law safeguards, the petitioner said.
Article Summary: An all-women NGO has appealed to the Supreme Court not to confer trans-women, biological males identifying as females, the spectrum of constitutional rights guaranteed to biological women. ‘Women’s Declaration International India’ through senior advocate Amit Sibal told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that ‘self-professed or socio-cultural gender identity or certificate or document cannot change a person’’

Article Title: 'They will fly': MEA on direct India-Taiwan flights after Pakistan blocks airspace over 'One-China' policy

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Wednesday indicated that direct air connectivity between India and Taiwan could be explored, amid reports that Pakistan has barred Taiwanese airlines from using its airspace under its “One China” policy.“My sense is, if there are direct flights then they will fly,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said when asked about the possibility of direct flights between India and Taiwan.The remarks came after Pakistan reportedly restricted Taiwanese carriers from using its airspace, in a move that highlights Islamabad's support for Beijing's position on Taiwan.Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif confirmed the country's position to Bloomberg News, saying its aviation policy permits only mainland Chinese airlines to fly over its airspace.“The aviation division follows the One China policy — only mainland China is allowed,” Asif said.“We have permitted only Chinese airlines to fly over Pakistan,” he added.Pakistan is the first country reported to have taken such a step against Taiwanese carriers. Bloomberg, citing flight-tracking data, reported that China Airlines Ltd and EVA Airways Corp had not flown over Pakistani airspace since the morning of October 25.The restriction came to light after aviation observers noticed that some Taiwanese flights had begun taking longer routes to reach Europe, flying entirely over Russian airspace since the weekend.According to Flightradar24 data, a China Airlines flight from Taipei to Rome on October 24 flew through Russian airspace, bypassing its earlier route through India, Pakistan and Turkmenistan.The move comes as China continues to urge other countries to support its claim that Taiwan is part of its territory. Beijing considers Taiwan a part of China, while Taipei maintains that the island is self-governed and rejects Beijing's claim.Pakistan's decision also underlines its close ties with China, which Islamabad has described as an “iron-clad friendship”. The two countries have maintained an “all-weather” partnership since establishing diplomatic relations in 1951.In January, Pakistan described Taiwan as an “inalienable part” of China and reiterated its commitment to the One China principle.

The remarks came after Pakistan reportedly restricted Taiwanese carriers from using its airspace. Pakistan is the first country reported to have taken such a step against Taiwanese carriers.

Article Title: 'Commit to ballot paper': Congress dares PM Modi after his 'how many seats' swipe over MLC results

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday took a swipe at the Congress over its dismal performance in the MLC polls held across four states. The grand old party which failed to win a single seat in the polls, hit back at PM Modi over his “ballot paper” remark and challenged him to commit to holding all future Lok Sabha and assembly elections using ballot papers.The back-and-forth began when the Prime Minister in a post on X, wrote, "MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states - Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?"Congress Rajya Sabha member Pawan Khera hit back at PM Modi, asking him to demonstrate confidence in the BJP’s prowess by committing to ballot paper voting in all future Lok Sabha and assembly elections.In a post on X, Khera demanded the suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the restoration of 13.3 crore voters "deleted illegally"."If Narendra Modi is so confident that EVMs have no bearing on election results, let him prove his confidence in the BJP’s electoral prowess through action, not rhetoric," he wrote."1. Article Title: Supreme Court says legality of EC's 'logical discrepancy' checks in SIR remains undecided
Article Text:

What is the ‘logical discrepancy’ category

The Supreme Court on Wednesday clarified that it has not yet delivered a final ruling on the Election Commission of India ’s (ECI) use of the “logical discrepancy” category to flag voters’ details during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said its earlier decision allowing the Election Commission to use the category in West Bengal was only an interim measure. It also clarified that the court’s ruling on the SIR exercise in Bihar had not settled every legal question surrounding the revision process.The clarification came during a hearing on a petition alleging a lack of transparency in notices issued to voters during the ongoing SIR exercise in Delhi. Senior advocate D S Naidu, appearing for the Election Commission, had argued that the court had examined all stages of the SIR process and upheld its validity.Justice Bagchi rejected the suggestion that the earlier proceedings had conclusively settled the legality of the logical discrepancy category.“Bihar is not a final determination of every question arising in these proceedings. In Bihar, the Election Commission had not initially undertaken logical discrepancy as a category.We permitted it as an interim arrangement in West Bengal. We have not finally adjudicated upon the legality of the logical discrepancy exercise,” Justice Bagchi was quoted as saying by the news agency PTI.The judge also cautioned against treating oral observations made during hearings as final judicial decisions, particularly in sensitive cases."We do not wish to make further comments because observations in sensitive matters are sometimes taken out of context. These observations are not conclusive. There is a difficulty when judicial observations are repeatedly cited out of context as if every issue has already been decided," he said.During the SIR exercise, the Election Commission uses the “logical discrepancy” category to flag inconsistencies in voters’ records. These discrepancies are identified through ERONet, the poll panel’s centralised technology platform, which uses automated checks to examine electoral data.Such flags can arise when information in a voter’s profile or details linking family members appear inconsistent with mathematical, biological or clerical records. The category is intended to identify entries that require scrutiny.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday clarified that it has not yet delivered a final ruling on the Election Commission of India ’s use of the ‘logical discrepancy’ category. The clarification came during a hearing on a petition alleging a lack of transparency in notices issued to voters during the ongoing SIR exercise in Delhi.

GURGAON: The Indian Patent Office has rejected a patent application by US-based Global Alliance for TB Drug Development for BPaL, a life-saving tuberculosis therapy, citing lack of novelty and inventive step. The decision could allow domestic drugmakers to launch cheaper generic versions in India and other high-burden countries, health experts said.Govt provides BPaL, a combination of bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid, free under National TB Elimination Programme. However, treatment costs remain a challenge. The six-month all-oral regimen is shorter than older treatments and reduces patients’ compliance burden. More than 15,000 patients have begun BPaLM, which adds moxifloxacin, under the programme.Pre-grant oppositions were filed separately by Sankalp Rehabilitation Trust’s Eldred Tellis and TB survivor Ganesh Acharya, supported by Lawyers’ Collective and Médécins Sans Frontières Access Campaign; and Delhi Network of Positive People, supported by Third World Network.Patent Controller upheld grounds of lack of novelty, lack of inventive step, non-patentability and insufficient disclosure, refusing application under Sec 15 of Patents Act.Opponents argued the combination and its use in a shorter regimen had been disclosed in scientific research dating to 2015.The opposition invoked Sections 3(d), 3(e) and 3(i), which restrict patents on new uses of known substances, exclude mere admixtures and methods of medical treatment. All four grounds were upheld.TB Alliance had earlier licensed generic firms, including Macleods Pharma and Lupin, to manufacture pretomanid for BPaL in India, though health activists called the agreements restrictive. This could widen the supplier pool.
Article Summary: Patent application by US-based Global Alliance for TB Drug Development for BPaL rejected. Decision could allow domestic drugmakers to launch cheaper generic versions in India and other high-burden countries. Govt provides BPaLM, a combination of bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid, free under National TB Elimination Programme.

Article Title: Junk food’s impact may go beyond the weighing scale
Article Text:
Junk food impact on health

NEW DELHI: A packet of chips after school, a cookie between meals or a burger as a treat may seem harmless. But a new study suggests that eating more ultra-processed foods may be linked to changes in how children’s brains respond to food, as well as greater gains in body fat over the following year.Published in JAMA Network Open this month, the study followed 46 children who were at a healthy weight at the start. Researchers found that children who got a larger share of their daily calories from ultra-processed foods (UPFs) showed stronger responses in a brain region linked to reward, motivation and habit formation when they saw pictures of tempting foods such as cookies and French fries.These stronger brain responses were linked to greater increases in body mass index (BMI) and body fat over the next year. Children who ate more UPFs also showed an increase in waist size.The findings raise a new concern in the debate over childhood obesity: could the way children’s brains respond to food be part of the link between eating highly processed foods and gaining weight?Dr Arun Gupta, convenor of Nutrition Advocacy in Public Interest (NAPi) and co-author of the 2025 Lancet series on ultra-processed foods, said the findings should prompt a closer look at the foods children eat and how these products are marketed to them.He said repeated exposure to highly appealing foods could encourage habitual eating.The study, however, did not prove that children become addicted to food or that junk food directly changes their brains.The researchers also found that sugar alone may not explain the link. Many ultra-processed foods combine fat and carbohydrates, which can trigger a strong reward response in the brain. However, when researchers accounted for added-sugar intake, the link between UPF consumption and brain response weakened, suggesting that several factors may be involved.The findings come amid calls for tighter restrictions on advertising foods high in fat, sugar and salt (HFSS) to children. NAPi has sought amendments to the Press Council of India’s Norms of Journalistic Conduct 2022 to prohibit such advertising. The Press Council referred the proposal to the Union health ministry in May 2024, sought comments in June 2025 and sent a reminder in 2026, but NAPi says it is still awaiting a response.It has also written to the information and broadcasting ministry.Although the study was conducted in the US and its findings cannot be directly extrapolated to Indian children, it raises a key question: should tackling childhood obesity also mean addressing the advertising and food environments that shape children’s choices?
Article Summary: Eating more ultra-processed foods may be linked to changes in how children’s brains respond to food. Study followed 46 children who were at a healthy weight at the start of the study. Children who ate more UPFs also showed an increase in waist size. Findings raise a new concern in the debate over childhood obesity.

Article Title: Isro to launch NVS-03 on Oct 30, but NavIC has a long way to go
Article Text:
NVS-03 is the third satellite in Isro’s next-generation navigation series

Why the launch matters

A troubled programme

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Still a long road

BENGALURU: Isro will launch its next navigation satellite, NVS-03, aboard the GSLV-F18 rocket on Friday (Oct 30) at 11.51 pm from the Second Launch Pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.GSLV-F18 is the 20th flight of India’s Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV). The mission is a crucial attempt to rebuild India’s ailing NavIC navigation constellation, which currently lacks enough operational satellites to provide standalone positioning services.The roughly 50-metre rocket, with a lift-off mass of about 420 tonnes, will place the approximately 2,250-kg NVS-03 into a geosynchronous transfer orbit with a perigee (closest point to Earth) of 170 km, apogee (farthest point from Earth) of 37,023 km and inclination of 20.75°.NVS-03 is the third satellite in Isro’s next-generation navigation series, designed to ensure continuity of the services of the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System, now called Navigation with Indian Constellation, or NavIC.NavIC is intended to provide Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) services across India and up to about 1,500 km beyond the country’s landmass, reducing dependence on foreign navigation systems.“NVS-03 carries an indigenous atomic clock alongside procured clocks and introduces the L1 signal, in addition to the existing L5 and S signals,” Isro said. The addition is expected to widen compatibility with more user devices and strengthen NavIC’s civilian and strategic utility.But the launch comes at a time when NavIC is operating below its minimum requirement. Earlier this year, union minister Jitendra Singh told Parliament: “After completion of mission life (10 years) of IRNSS-1F, presently the NavIC constellation has three satellites — IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1I and NVS-01 — for providing PNT services.To provide basic positioning service, a minimum of four operational satellites are required in orbit.” The govt acknowledged that, as a result, “the NavIC constellation cannot provide standalone positioning service, however timing service is functional.”NavIC’s difficulties stem from a combination of ageing satellites, atomic-clock failures and a failed replenishment mission. IRNSS-1F completed its 10-year mission life in March 2026; soon after, Isro said its procured onboard atomic clock stopped functioning, removing the satellite from navigation service.The more immediate setback was NVS-02, launched on Jan 29, 2025 aboard GSLV-F15. Although the satellite separated successfully and deployed its solar panels, it could not perform the orbit-raising manoeuvres needed to move from its elliptical transfer orbit to its designated circular orbit.An Isro apex committee traced the anomaly to the spacecraft’s pyro system. It found that the drive signal did not reach the pyro valve in the oxidiser line of the orbit-raising engine, preventing the engine from firing. The committee concluded that the most likely cause was disengagement of at least one contact in each of the main and redundant connector paths.Isro said the panel recommended corrective measures to enhance redundancy and improve the reliability of pyro-system operations, and that these recommendations have already been implemented.NVS-03’s successful launch would raise the number of navigation-capable satellites, but it will not by itself restore NavIC to full operational strength. The spacecraft must first complete orbit-raising manoeuvres, reach its designated orbit and be validated for service.The govt has said NVS-04 and NVS-05 are in an advanced stage of realisation, meaning further launches will be needed before NavIC regains a robust, redundant constellation.NavIC’s return to standalone positioning service depends not only on NVS-03 reaching orbit, but on Isro executing the post-launch operations that failed for NVS-02, and on the timely induction of the satellites that follow.
Article Summary: NVS-03 is the third satellite in Isro’s next-generation navigation series. It is designed to ensure continuity of the services of the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System. NavIC is intended to provide Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) services across India.

Article Title: IN-SPACe picks 6 AI space projects for grants of up to Rs 1-cr each
Article Text:
Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre

BENGALURU: Space regulator-cum-promoter Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) has selected six private space-sector entities for seed-fund grants under its AI INSPIRED programme, which aims to encourage the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in space technology.The projects span precision landing, space situational awareness, debris detection, satellite servicing and refuelling, automated target recognition, and spacecraft autonomy. Two other entities have been selected for mentorship and technical support, including access to Isro facilities for technology validation.The programme, announced in Feb 2026 under IN-SPACe’s Seed Fund Scheme, has a total outlay of up to Rs 6 crore, with each selected entity eligible for a grant of up to Rs 1 crore. The funding is intended to help start-ups and micro and small enterprises develop AI-based solutions for space applications.Among the selected projects, Agnikul Cosmos will develop an edge AI-enabled vision-based terminal navigation module for precision landing. The technology is aimed at improving navigation during the final stages of a landing manoeuvre.Digantara has been selected for its Agentic RSO Evaluation Suite (ARES), while EON Space Labs will develop an intelligent optical payload using field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based edge AI.The latter project aims to enable real-time space situational awareness and detection of space debris.OrbitAid Aerospace will work on machine-learning-assisted pose estimation algorithms for on-orbit servicing and refuelling. Such algorithms can help spacecraft determine their relative positions and orientations, an important requirement for operations involving approaching, docking with or servicing another spacecraft.Omnipresent Robot Technologies has been selected for an automated target recognition project covering applications such as defence and docking. TakeMeToSpace will work on adaptive spacecraft autonomy through an AI modernisation programme for attitude determination and control systems (ADCS), which help establish a spacecraft's orientation and maintain its intended direction.IN-SPACe has also selected Foucault Private Limited and AkashaVeda Technologies for mentorship and technical support, although they are not listed among the six seed-fund grantees.Foucault will work on an autonomous collision avoidance system for spacecraft using AI and machine learning. AkashaVeda’s project focuses on AI-based mission management, covering both onboard and ground operations. The two entities will receive opportunities to use IN-SPACe and Isro facilities to validate their technologies. They will also be considered for technology transfer from the Department of Space.As per IN-SPACe, the initiative is part of its efforts to expand private participation in India’s space sector by supporting the development of indigenous technologies and products.
Article Summary: The projects span precision landing, space situational awareness, debris detection, satellite servicing and refuelling, automated target recognition, and spacecraft autonomy. The funding is intended to help start-ups and micro and small enterprises develop AI-based solutions for space applications.

Article Title: Guess how many Congress won: PM Modi
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in an X post, mocked the Congress party for its failure to secure a single seat in the Legislative Council Elections in four states despite the use of ballot paper

NEW DELHI: “Guess how many seats Congress won?” asked PM Narendra Modi Wednesday, turning to biting sarcasm — and adding a playful emoji to boot — to rip into the opposition party as it stared at a rout in the MLC elections held through ballot papers for 28 seats across four states.“MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states — Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?” Modi said on X.It was at once a taunt that underscored Congress’s continuing troubles and a rebuke to the opposition party’s claim that BJP's successes are because of the manipulation of EVMs and electoral rolls.What added to Congress’s embarrassment was that it was swept aside on all four seats in Karnataka, where it is in office, by BJP-JDS combine.As the results emerged, with counting for some seats still on , BJP president Nitin Nabin also emphasised that Congress had drawn a blank. People have decisively rejected its anarchic politics, he added.The results brought a mix of relief and joy to BJP as Congress and its allies have hit the streets and planned a campaign to win over people through their charge that EC has fixed the SIR of electoral rolls to BJP’s advantage.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi mocked the Congress party for its failure to secure a single seat in the Legislative Council Elections in four states. It was at once a taunt that underscored Congress’s continuing troubles and a rebuke to the opposition party's claim that BJP's successes are because of the manipulation of EVMs and electoral rolls.

Article Title: Healthy citizens essential to achieve goal of developed India: Anupriya Patel
Article Text:
File photo: Union Minister Anupriya Patel

NEW DELHI: Healthy citizens are essential to achieve the goal of Viksit Bharat, Union minister of state for health and family welfare Anupriya Patel said Wednesday while presenting govt’s health roadmap for a developed India by 2047.Delivering the guest of honour address at the Times Network India Health Summit & Awards 2026, Patel said the health sector budget has almost quadrupled from around Rs 37,000 crore in 2013-2014 while out-of-pocket expenditure had fallen from over 64% of total healthcare spending to around 43%. She added that Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana had played a significant role in this.She said national telemedicine network ‘e-Sanjeevani’ enables citizens to get remote consultation from specialist doctors, easing pressure on hospitals and benefiting the elderly and women.Delhi health minister Pankaj Singh said the state govt’s goal is to provide better healthcare facilities closer to home. He said four new hospitals would open in Delhi next year.Union minister Prataprao Jadhav said, “The debate between traditional and modern medicine shouldn’t be limited to choosing one method over another. The primary objective of healthcare should be to provide patients with the right care tailored to their needs.”
Article Summary: Health sector budget has almost quadrupled from around Rs 37,000 crore in 2013-2014. Out-of-pocket expenditure had fallen from over 64% of total healthcare spending to around 43%. She said national telemedicine network ‘e-Sanjeevani’ enables citizens to get remote consultation from specialist doctors.

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi Wednesday called for tighter monitoring of welfare schemes and infrastructure projects, asking chief secretaries to review their implementation with DMs every month. He also directed ministries and state govts to resolve bottlenecks in mission mode, strengthen coordination and fix accountability to ensure timely delivery of benefits and completion of projects.Chairing the monthly IT-based Pragati meeting, PM is learnt to have raised concerns over delay in land acquisition for projects and slow progress in redevelopment of Ahmedabad railway station.He directed agencies to complete the redevelopment project by Aug 2027 at any cost, an official said.In an official release, PMO said Modi emphasised that governance must focus more on outcomes than outlays, ensuring that public expenditure translates into tangible improvements in people’s livesModi reviewed infrastructure projects worth over Rs 16,000 crore covering railways, PM Ekta Malls and bulk drug parks across 31 states and Union territories.He underlined that PM Ekta Malls should provide markets for local products, strengthen livelihoods of artisans and help them expand their enterprises.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi Wednesday called for tighter monitoring of welfare schemes and infrastructure projects. He also directed ministries and state govts to resolve bottlenecks in mission mode. He is learnt to have raised concerns over delay in land acquisition for projects and slow progress in redevelopment of Ahmedabad railway station.
